reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) shows that adding more elements promotes random alloy formation under limited mobility, but it does not provide data on lattice strain, diffusion barriers, or high-temperature stability against coarsening. E3 mentions thermal stability up to 1173 K but lacks mechanistic detail linking it to sluggish diffusion. Thus, the core mechanistic premises are unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Multiple principal elements in HEA nanoparticles create extensive lattice strain and local energy barriers
These barriers kinetically suppress atomic diffusion (sluggish diffusion)
Sluggish diffusion prevents coarsening, phase segregation, and growth during high-temperature exposure
Low-temperature or low-mobility synthesis is required to freeze in the disordered state
Binary or fewer-element nanoparticles lack this stabilizing effect and will sinter/segregate more
